note: CENSUS measurement questions. These are the specific statistical unknowns that must be resolved to move affected-population and revenue estimates from NOT_YET_MEASURED to a defensible range. Ordered by information value (decision impact).

questions.metric: What fraction of active Energy Performance Contracts in EU-27 result in M&V settlement disputes requiring third-party resolution or multi-round negotiation, per annual settlement cycle?
availableSources: IPMVP body (EVF) dispute rate data (unknown availability)
National EED Article 5 implementation reports (may contain EPC dispute statistics)
Qualitative interviews with ESCO energy managers (WITNESS)
questions.method: WITNESS qualitative interviews (≥15 ESCO project managers) + industry association survey
questions.decisionBoundary: If dispute rate > 5%, the affected population is commercially viable (100+ events/year at lower EPC count). If < 1%, the addressable market may be too thin for a standalone product. Order-of-magnitude precision is sufficient.

witnessHandoff.targetPopulationDescription: Active EPC project managers and energy managers at ESCO firms operating in EU-27
witnessHandoff.sampleDesign: Purposive sampling: 15-25 ESCO project managers from at least 3 EU countries, minimum 3 different building types. Not probability sample — cannot produce population CI but sufficient to establish order-of-magnitude and qualitative mechanism.

questions.notes: HIGHEST PRIORITY UNKNOWN for HeatProof. The existence of a EUR 5K-50K M&V verifier market implies disputes occur and are costly — but rate is unknown. A 2-day LinkedIn outreach to EUROACE members could produce qualitative answers. Decision: do before any further product development.

questions.metric: How many distinct Balancing Service Providers (BSPs) are registered in the ENTSO-E transparency platform for EU-27 TSO flexibility markets, and what is the average number of physical sites per BSP?
availableSources: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform BSP registration data (PUBLIC_FREE, available now)
National TSO BSP registries (Ofgem, BNetzA, RTE, ELIA — PUBLIC)
questions.method: Download ENTSO-E Transparency Platform data, extract BSP table, count distinct BSPs, research average sites/BSP from a sample
questions.decisionBoundary: If enrolled sites < 500: too thin for standalone product without custom sales. If 2,000+: sufficient density for scalable product. WITHIN_50PCT precision distinguishes these scenarios.
questions.notes: HIGH INFORMATION VALUE, ZERO COST. Data is freely available from ENTSO-E. Download and process before any further commercial assumption. Estimated 2-hour task.

questions.metric: How many qualifying high-stakes B2B procurement decisions (capital equipment or complex B2B software, >EUR 50K) does a typical EU manufacturing enterprise with 50+ employees make per year?
availableSources: ECB/EBA survey on B2B procurement patterns (may exist)
Purchasing management association (CIPS, BME) surveys on procurement frequency
WITNESS qualitative interviews with procurement managers
questions.method: WITNESS qualitative: 20+ procurement managers across manufacturing and regulated sectors. Survey asking annual qualifying decision count by value tier.
questions.decisionBoundary: Current assumption: 2-10 events/enterprise/year. If true value is <1: eligible event population is too small. If >15: much larger than assumed. Factor-of-two precision narrows the 100K-500K range to something actionable.

witnessHandoff.targetPopulationDescription: Procurement managers at EU manufacturing enterprises 50+ employees
witnessHandoff.sampleDesign: Purposive: 20+ procurement managers across at least 4 manufacturing NACE subsectors (C20, C22, C24, C28). Not probability sample.
witnessHandoff.precisionTarget: Determine whether central tendency is <2, 2-5, 5-10, or >10 events/enterprise/year

questions.notes: The events/enterprise/year assumption is the binding sensitivity for DOGFOOD B market size. Without this, the 100K-500K range has a 5× width that prevents any commercial precision. WITNESS survey is the right method.

questions.metric: For qualifying B2B procurement decisions in EU manufacturing, in what fraction of cases is adequate independent performance evidence unavailable, causing material procurement friction?
availableSources: WITNESS qualitative interviews (cannot produce CI, but establishes mechanism and rough order of magnitude)
G2/Gartner category coverage data (inverse: categories with review platforms ≠ evidence gap)
questions.method: WITNESS qualitative interviews (same sample as cmq-b01). Ask directly: 'In what share of your qualifying purchases was the evidence available to you before purchase decision inadequate?'
questions.decisionBoundary: If <10% of events: niche problem for very specialist products. If >30%: widespread structural problem. Order-of-magnitude sufficient for initial investment decision.

witnessHandoff.targetPopulationDescription: Same as cmq-b01 procurement manager sample
witnessHandoff.sampleDesign: Piggyback on cmq-b01 interview guide. Add questions on evidence gap experience.
strataNeeded: Product category (capital equipment vs software vs regulated material)

questions.notes: Combine with cmq-b01 WITNESS protocol for efficiency. Counter-evidence in TERRAIN: large enterprises (Fortune 500) have procurement teams and analyst subscriptions that partially address this. Problem may be concentrated in mid-market.

questions.metric: What is the maximum willingness-to-pay per M&V settlement event for an ESCO or building owner using HeatProof?
availableSources: Current M&V verifier market rate (EUR 5K-50K/engagement) as ceiling benchmark
questions.method: MERCURY: prepayment experiment — present HeatProof offering to 5+ ESCO project managers with specific pricing options. Observe actual payment behaviour. Price-discovery is Mercury mission, not CENSUS.
questions.decisionBoundary: Financial model scenario EUR 89/month midpoint needs Mercury validation. If WTP < EUR 20/month: scenario is too optimistic. If WTP > EUR 200/month: significant upside. Mercury must determine.
questions.notes: MERCURY HANDOFF. CENSUS acknowledges this question but cannot answer it. Price determination requires buying behaviour, not population counting. The EUR 5K-50K verifier market rate provides a useful ceiling benchmark.
